title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ (2026)
author: Asha Patel
summary: Comprehensive sales enablement playbook covering messaging, competitor positioning, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case study templates, and a security FAQ intended for sales, solutions engineering, and GTM leadership.
content:
Purpose

This playbook equips Redwood Inference sales, solutions engineering, and GTM partners with consistent positioning, competitive battlegrounds, pitch deck guidance, pricing rules-of-thumb, reusable case study templates, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this as the canonical source for customer conversations and enablement assets.

Audience

- Account Executives (AEs) and Sales Engineers (SEs)
- Growth and Partner teams
- GTM leadership and sales ops

Key positioning & messaging (elevator + proof points)

Elevator pitch (15–30s):
- "Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers production-grade LLM serving with predictable latency, lower unit cost, and flexible deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). We help engineering teams ship LLM features reliably and economically without building a bespoke serving stack."

Primary value propositions (customer-facing bullets):
- Predictable performance: SLO-backed latency and throughput for production workloads; optimized kernels and autoscaling reduce tail latency.
- Cost control: intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles that reduce tokens/second cost while preserving quality.
- Deployment flexibility: same API and tooling across hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and VPC/on-prem private deployments.
- Reliability & fallbacks: multi-variant routing, regional failover, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants keep apps online.
- Observability & ops: token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, and rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback).

Messaging by persona

- ML/Backend Engineers: focus on SDKs, runtime performance (throughput, latency), deterministic behavior, and rollback/route controls.
- Platform/Infra Teams: emphasize capacity isolation (Dedicated), autoscaling policies, and integration with existing KMS/VPC controls.
- Product/PMs: outcome-oriented messaging — faster time-to-market, predictable unit economics, and quality guardrails for regressions.

Competitive brief (high level)

Primary competitors: generic cloud AI endpoints (major cloud providers), LLM API vendors, and inference infra vendors.

Quick comparison table (text)

- Redwood Inference: unified runtime + ops (hosted/dedicated/private), cost controls, high observability, production-first APIs.
- Cloud AI managed endpoints: deep infra integration & global regions; often higher per-token cost, limited deployment abstraction across private deployments.
- LLM API vendors: easy onboarding and model access; may lack predictable performance and enterprise deployment options.
- Inference infra vendors/self-hosted runtimes: more control and lower opex at scale; requires heavy engineering investment and ops maturity.

Competitive differentiators and battlecard bullets

- Win themes vs cloud providers: "We give you a consistent developer experience across hosted and private deployments and better unit economics for production inference."
- Win themes vs LLM API vendors: "We offer production SLAs, dedicated capacity, and enterprise controls absent from consumer-focused APIs."
- Win themes vs infra vendors: "You get the runtime and orchestration without building or operating the stack—fast time-to-value plus enterprise primitives."

Top objections & rebuttals

1) "We can run this in-house cheaper."
- Rebuttal: Show TCO model highlighting engineering FTEs, ops burden, and slower time-to-market. Provide example: mid-market customer reduced per-token cost by ~30% after enabling batching/cache and avoided hiring a 3-person infra team for 12 months.

2) "Vendor lock-in / data security concerns."
- Rebuttal: Explain private deployment option, VPC/on-prem packaging, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logging. Offer reference architecture and customer references for similar regulated customers.

Pitch deck guidance (slide-by-slide)

Recommended deck length: 10–12 slides for discovery/initial meetings. Tailor for enterprise (include security/compliance slides) or SMB (focus on speed & cost).

Suggested slide flow and content:
1) Title + one-line value prop (use elevator pitch)
2) Problem statement: quantifiable pain (latency, cost, ops)
3) Why now: model improvements + adoption patterns
4) Redwood solution: high-level architecture diagram (hosted/dedicated/private) and one-sentence differentiator
5) Key benefits (latency, cost, reliability, deployments) — 3–4 concise bullets with proof points
6) Demo or screenshots: console, latency/cost graph, rollout UI
7) Architecture & deployment options: hosted, dedicated, private (with short bullets per option)
8) Pricing overview & buying motion: usage-based, reserved, enterprise licensing (high-level numbers, see pricing guidance)
9) Security & compliance: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs, penetration testing cadence
10) Customer stories / proof (2 short case studies; include metrics)
11) Next steps: trial onboarding checklist, pilot KPIs, stakeholders
12) Appendix: detailed benchmarks, SLA language, contract contacts

Pitch demo checklist for SEs

- Confirm customer sample workload (tokens/sec, sequence lengths, concurrency).
- Prepare a quick perf comparison: baseline latencies, token cost estimate, and predicted gains from batching/quantization.
- Show console: model routes, rollout controls, token-level analytics, and tracing.
- Validate security controls: show VPC controls, KMS integration, and audit log examples (if applicable).

Pricing guidance (rules of thumb)

High level pricing constructs (sales talking points):
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per-token generation + per-embedding rates), tiered volume discounts at predictable thresholds.
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved capacity pricing (monthly/annual commit) with burst and autoscale; typically used when predictable throughput is required.
- Redwood Private: platform licensing + support and optional deployment/setup fee for on-prem/VPC installs.

Negotiation levers and thresholds

- Volume discounts: standard bands at 1M, 10M, 100M tokens (example tiers; check pricing sheet for current rates).
- Commit length: multi-year or annual commitments may unlock 10–25% discounts depending on capacity.
- Security/compliance add-ons: premium pricing for additional retention, compliance packages, or HSM/KMS management.
- Enterprise support SLAs: higher SLAs and on-call support are add-on items.

Packaging & recommended selling motions

- Proof-of-Value (PoV) pilot: 4–6 weeks, includes sample workload integration, benchmark run, and pilot KPIs (latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate).
- Mid-market: hosted usage with guidance to move to Dedicated at predictable volume thresholds.
- Large enterprise/SLED: pitch Private for regulated workloads with professional services for deployment.

Case study templates & sample vignettes

Case study template (fields to collect during reference calls):
- Customer name (permissioned):
- Industry & size:
- Problem / trigger:
- Solution (Redwood product & deployment mode):
- Implementation timeline and owners:
- Key metrics & outcomes (latency improvement, cost delta, throughput change, uptime):
- Quotes & testimonials:
- Contact for reference (if permitted)

Example: Fintech scale-up (short vignette)
- Customer: FinFlow (Series B payments startup)
- Challenge: 300ms median latency requirement for transaction summaries at 50 concurrent users and strict PII handling.
- Solution: Dedicated capacity + KV caching + quantized model variant; private VPC peering for PII workflows.
- Outcome: Median latency down from 680ms to 210ms; per-request cost reduced by ~28%; met PCI-scope requirements through private deployment and audit logs.

Example: Marketplaces platform (short vignette)
- Customer: ShopMatch (mid-market)
- Challenge: Embedding costs and throughput spikes from search/recall features.
- Solution: Hosted API + intelligent batching, caching embeddings, and model recommendations for embedding quantization.
- Outcome: Embedding pipeline cost reduced by ~45% and 3x throughput increase during peak indexing windows.

Security FAQ for prospects (top-of-funnel answers)

Q: Where does customer data live and how is it accessed?
A: By default hosted workloads are stored in the regional cloud chosen by the customer; for regulated customers Redwood offers Dedicated or Private deployments. Access to customer data is strictly controlled via RBAC and audit logs. For Private deployments data remains in the customer's VPC or on-prem environment per contract.

Q: Do you retain prompts or model outputs?
A: Retention policies are configurable. For customers requiring zero-retention, Private deployments or Dedicated with configured retention rules can be used. We provide deletion tooling and export APIs.

Q: How is data encrypted?
A: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+/mTLS where applicable) and at rest using customer-managed keys (KMS) or Redwood-managed encryption. We support HSM-backed keys for customers requiring hardware roots of trust.

Q: Can we run Redwood in our VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes — Redwood Private provides a deployable control plane for VPC and on-prem installs. We also offer a hybrid model for separating sensitive workloads.

Q: What compliance certifications do you hold?
A: We maintain SOC 2 Type II; customers can request compliance packages and additional audit evidence under an NDA. We provide architecture patterns for GDPR, HIPAA, and other regional requirements; actual certification for specific workloads may need a Private deployment.

Q: How do you handle incident response and breach notification?
A: We have a published incident response playbook that meets industry-standard timelines. Customers under enterprise contracts receive direct communication paths and support for forensic artifacts.

Q: Do you perform penetration testing and vulnerability scanning?
A: Yes — we run regular internal and third-party pen tests along with automated vulnerability scanning in our CI/CD pipelines. Reports are available under NDA.

Q: How is key management handled?
A: Customers can bring their own keys via integrations with major KMS providers or opt for Redwood-managed keys. HSM options are available for Private deployments.

Sales playbook & next steps (practical workflows)

1) Discovery call checklist:
   - Confirm persona and stakeholders (engineering, security, procurement).
   - Capture workload shape: QPS, concurrency, median/95p seq length, expected monthly tokens.
   - Identify must-have compliance requirements (e.g., data residency, retention, logging).
   - Agree on pilot KPIs and timeline (4–6 weeks recommended).

2) SE onboarding steps for PoV:
   1. Provision test environment (hosted or dedicated pilot).
   2. Run baseline benchmark with customer sample workload.
   3. Apply batching/caching/quantization recommendations and re-run benchmarks.
   4. Produce pilot report with expected run-rate cost, latency improvements, and recommended next steps.

3) Contracting & procurement tips:
   - Use standard SOW templates for Private deployments; include acceptance criteria tied to pilot KPIs.
   - Highlight data processing addendum and security appendix early in procurement.

Appendix: sample benchmark summary (how to present numbers)

- Always show both latency (p50/p95) and cost per 1k tokens before/after optimization.
- Include concurrency and sequencing assumptions.
- Provide an explicit ops effort estimate to self-host vs. Redwood-managed (FTE months).
